# Paragraph shading and spacing

Original controls generated by `tools/shading_spacing_fixture.py` with
python-docx (MIT), independently of the renderer. Four DOCX files cover
compatibility modes 14/15 and following before-spacing of 6/30pt. Each has
15 cases on 16 pages. The PDFs were exported by the reference application from the schema-valid sources. No corpus artwork or fonts are included.

`tools/shading_spacing_reference.py` extracts colored PDF path bounds and
label baselines; the JSON references pin both source and PDF SHA-256 hashes.
The browser test checks every native page within 0.2pt vertically, plus editable
open, exact no-edit package preservation, insertion/export/reopen and exact undo.

The reference application excludes spacing around isolated shaded paragraphs. Adjacent shaded
paragraphs with equal horizontal bounds share the collapsed gap: the preceding
fill covers its allocated after-spacing and the following fill covers the
remainder. Different colors do not overlap. Contextual spacing is respected.
Different horizontal bounds and page breaks interrupt the shared gap. Bordered
paragraphs retain their border-frame bounds; table-cell cases are included.

Relevant clauses: ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.12 (`ind`), 17.3.1.24 (`pBdr`),
17.3.1.31 (`shd`), 17.3.1.33 (`spacing`). The exact gap-paint allocation is
native reference compatibility evidence, not a claim that the standard specifies
this pixel geometry. Horizontal border/indent geometry beyond these controls
is not certified by the vertical-bound comparison.
